newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF BARCELONA PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF BARCELONA PLAYERS.

text.p: Pen pictures of the players most likely to play for Barcelona against Real Madrid in the Spanish first division game on Saturday:

Vitor Baia, goalkeeper, age 27. The Portuguese international keeper has fully justified his 800 million peseta ($6.34 million) transfer fee with a string of game-saving performances since moving from Porto in the close season,
Carlos Busquets, goalkeeper, age 29. Nearly ever-present last season, Busquets has had few chances to prove himself since the arrival of Baia.

Albert Ferrer, defender, 26. Right-sided defender who has reappeared since injury cut short his Euro 96 plans at the end of last season. Ferrer makes up for a lack of physical presence with a terrier-like determination in moves down the wing.

Abelardo Fernandez, defender, 26. An experienced Spanish international, Abelardo has hardly played this season because of the wealth of central defenders in the Barcelona line-up. Dangerous in the air, particularly at corners.
Laurent Blanc, defender, 31. The Frenchman was one of Johan Cruyff's last signings but has only recently come into the reckoning at the centre of Bobby Robson's defence.
Sergi Barjuan, defender, 24. A key factor down the left in both defence and attack, Sergi is one of the quickest men in the Spanish game and an instant first choice.
Miguel Angel Nadal, defender/midfielder, 30. Surprisingly skilful for a big man, Nadal's failure to hold down a regular place has seen him linked to English champions Manchester United.

Gheorghe Popescu, defender/midfielder, 29. Former Tottenham man who has been handed the captaincy of the Barcelona side after the departure of Jose Maria Bakero. Strong coming forward, Popescu is also a set-piece specialist.

Luis Enrique Martinez, defender/midfielder, 26. Energetic utility player who pops up in every position except goalkeeper and has blossomed -- primarily as an overlapping full-back -- since signing from Real Madrid in the close-season.
Josep Guardiola, midfielder, 25. Classy and intelligent, Guardiola has returned to favour under Robson after being sidelined by Cruyff.

Ivan de la Pena, midfielder, 20. The shaven-headed darling of the Camp Nou crowd is a superb passer and set-piece man. But a desire to do too much every time, and an apparent reluctance to tackle back mean that he is only likely to appear as a substitute if the game needs to be turned around.
Guillermo Amor, midfielder, 29. Came good at the end of last season with a series of crucial goals which earned him a Euro 96 slot, but has hardly played under Robson.
Roger Garcia, midfielder, 19. Roger has been left on the sidelines by the arrival of foreign stars after playing regularly under Cruyff.

Giovanni, midfielder/striker, 24. Traded Pele's number 10 shirt at Santos for the playmaker role at Barcelona. A fine finisher, and a particularly good header of the ball, Giovanni is the ideal foil to compatriot Ronaldo.
Luis Figo, striker, 24. Skilful Portuguese international who is at home down either the left or right wing. Has been linked to Real along with Popescu in recent transfer rumours.

Ronaldo, striker, 20. A series of sensational individual goals has made Ronaldo the undisputed king of the Spanish game, and has already gone a long way to justifying the then world record $20 million paid to PSV Eindhoven in the close season.

Juan Pizzi, striker 28. A naturalised Argentine who was Spain's top goalscorer while at Tenerife last season, Pizzi has been left in the shadow of Ronaldo since joining Barcelona. Tends to squander easy chances.
